A cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm is fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
The beam is made of structural steel with Young's modulus E = 200 000 MPa and has a constant second moment of area I = 1 200 000 mm⁴.
A downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end (x = L).
Use Euler–Bernoulli beam theory with the small-deflection, linear-elastic assumption.
The bending moment varies linearly along the span as M(x) = P·(L − x), equal to zero at the free end and P·L at the fixed end.
All calculations use the N–mm–MPa unit system.
Compute the slope (rotation) at the free end using θ(L) = P·L² / (2·E·I) and report it in radians and in degrees.
Compute the vertical deflection at the free end using δ(L) = P·L³ / (3·E·I) and report it in mm.
State the direction (sign) of both the slope and the deflection relative to the applied downward load.
